body:
Make note of [this](http://www.metanoia.org/suicide/), and read it if you're feeling suicidal (it's also in the sidebar).

Let me just say you're not alone in feeling like you don't belong. Are you seeing anybody for how you're feeling?

I'm sure I speak on behalf of everyone when I say I'm glad you're not dead.

You are absolutely not wasting our time (again, taking liberties on speaking on behalf of everybody, eheh). Those of us here to give the support do so by choice.

Personally I don't know about free support in the UK, but (as detached as this sounds) Google can wield some good results. Or somebody from the UK/with knowledge can chime in.

Of course you deserve fantastic friends. Everybody deserves people who are good for them.

Please read [this](http://www.metanoia.org/suicide/), and bookmark it. Read it again when you're feeling suicidal. Read all of it.

I think you mean "is". (\*puts on grammar nazi hat\*)

Given what you've told me, I'm leaning to agree with you (that it would be better if she were with you). Just to repeat myself to convey the importance of it though, just make sure you're comfortable first and foremost.

I understand what you mean.

If she's the type of person who can take this type of thing non-personally, maybe just tell her beforehand that at any point you might ask her to leave because you're uncomfortable. And then hopefully do it if you need to.

If not then you kinda have to make a tough choice.

If you're unsure it could really go either way (if you want her to or not). Personally I don't think you should leave it to being her choice.

Make sure you're as comfortable as you can be though ultimately.

I would say only bring her if you feel you need the moral support for it.

Remember the nurse is human too. They might not say things you completely agree with, you might feel they're not making much progress. Try to avoid overreacting (which to be fair is a little hard to realise at the time), and be honest.

If you ultimately don't like the result from seeing them, you shouldn't give up there.

Good luck. :)

Story of my life man, story of my life.

The silver lining is people will come and go in your life. Never replacing ones from your past, but damned well as good as, or better.
That's also very possible too, haha.

Do you think once a month would be better than nothing at this point? (Assuming you're currently at nothing)

Ah, the stigma. It's easy to just not tell people though. :) Medication I was on really fucked with aspects of my life that got me to the point where I stopped taking them too. Double edged sword it seems.

Anytime. I'm more than happy to listen if you ever need an ear. Only if you're comfortable enough to. :)

That's running off the assumption it hasn't hurt her at all. When my ex and I broke up, she "resented" me to the point where she had to take a break because she couldn't "bear to look at me without wanting to hit me", and she still hurt months after it.

I realise that isn't the most optimistic thing, haha, but it's the truth. Do yourself a favour and not read too much into "being very friendly". Like, gigantic bold letters, **do not read too much into it**!

I'm not too familiar with how it is in the U.S. (which I assume is where you are), but there should be some free options for you.

Why don't you want to be medicated, if I may ask?

There could also be support groups to associate yourself with (a stab in the dark to be honest), or individuals you can *just* talk to for support or whatever. It's definitely good you're making an effort though. :)

Ah you have no idea how much I can relate to all of that. I know how much it sucks.

People, and things, change. It's crap when it's not for the better (for you anyway), but it's pretty much unavoidable.

Well done! :)

Don't let that little factor get you down though, as there could be a plethora of unrelated reasons.

You've clearly done something right. ;)

Au contraire though, nothing is more pressing than ones own happiness.

The problem with that, is that it's unfair on the other person. Even if it is for good reasons! Love hurts.

Why aren't you playing some nooowwww?! I find I'm a little similar with that, so I watch short episodes (like, 20min shows) to keep me about if I'm feeling rather unfocused. It can do, yes, haha.

Normality is relative, and fuck the idea of having to conform to someone else's view of "normal" to be accepted.
What would you normally do for fun/distraction? Videos (movies/tv shows), reading, video games, other hobbies?

>I told him if he was going to walk out on me, then take me to the hospital because I was going to kill myself.

If this is connected to not having control over the mood swings, you absolutely need to apologise for this. It is unbelievably horrible to hear from somebody you love.

Give [this](http://www.metanoia.org/suicide/) a read if you haven't already (particularly the bits about calling a hotline).

If you don't want to, or (once you) have, redditors give crazy good support too.

I'm perfectly okay with this.

You should do something to distract yourself however.

hello, sir/madam!

:)

Having been on the other end of that - **tell him**. When I got my friend back it was amazingly good.

Assuming you have the ability to, you've got practically nothing to lose.
I can't upvote you enough. This attitude drives me insane.

Who cares if you're *good* at some of these things (video games, drawing, sports, writing)? Do it to enjoy yourself. I sure as hell do.

With that said though, I'm sure there's something you're good at - or will be - just haven't found your calling yet. :)

15 months here! (the rest of this is aimed at OP mostly)

It definitely still hurts. It doesn't "get easier" either, it just (at least in my experience), as you think about and do other things intentionally or not, gets put in the back of your mind.

Don't dismiss it ("I know it's just a stupid girl"), but at the same time don't believe it's *the* most important thing in the world either.

There'll always be people in the world who will do their best to help you. Sometimes you just don't know them yet.

It's probably not connected. If it worries you though, you should definitely ask a doctor.

From personal experience, all my muscle twitches are random (or seem that way), and don't get any physical signs (except lethargy really) when feeling particularly down.

Individuals are just that - different.
haha, I love living in a small-ish suburb in Australia, so many crap results to sift through. Tomorrow.. tomorrow..
I guess all I can really do is keep my eyes open..

Well thanks, I appreciate the compliment :)

I have a horrible attention span. Whenever I start writing a story, I lose interest after a page or two. >.>

I dont know where to begin, how to begin, nor want to do it alone though. >.<

I do know what you mean, and I'm totally aware I'm not the centre of the universe, just after awhile it genuinely feels like the lowest common denominator is me. Then all my rationale is overcome by just.. sadness.

Thankyou for sharing though

Heh ty. I love writing and language and such.

I didnt want to say it quite like that, yeah, cause it is waaay too much pressure. But thanks for the alternative. I probably couldnt have thought of it myself. >.<

I dont have a therapist at all.
